verified_claims: The next multiple of a_1 is always admissible, so the greedy sequence exists, is unbounded, and has gaps at most a_1.
For every m at least a_1, m is selected if and only if its prime support meets the prime support of every sequence term; a skipped m has an earlier coprime witness by greedy minimality.
For a selected x, the construction m=R p^k has exactly the primes at most a_1 that divide x and satisfies a_1 <= m < x whenever x has a prime factor greater than a_1.

The small-prime trace induction is non-circular: if the constructed m were skipped, its coprime witness b is strictly smaller than x, so the induction hypothesis for b contradicts disjointness from x.
Consequently, membership for every m at least a_1 depends only on which primes at most a_1 divide m.
With L equal to the product of the primes at most a_1, membership is L-periodic on the full half-line starting at a_1, not merely eventually periodic.
Every length-L integer block starting at or after a_1 contains the same positive number T of terms, and the endpoint a_n+L is selected; hence a_(n+T)=a_n+L for every n.
The supplied trace experiment was rerun and reported 19,585 tested large-prime terms with no failures; this is consistent evidence and is not used as proof.
summary: The proposed solution is complete and correct. Its key descent lemma handles the threshold a_1, large-prime erasure, and induction order rigorously, and the resulting modular membership periodicity is correctly converted into the required index translation for all n, including n=1.
transfer_assessment: Reusable: characterize a greedy increasing sequence as the ordered scan of all objects compatible with the eventual selected family; a skipped object then carries an earlier incompatibility witness.
Reusable: reduce infinite prime-support states to a finite trace by constructing a smaller exact-trace representative above the initial threshold and applying minimal-counterexample induction.
Reusable: once membership is periodic by value from the initial threshold, count one complete residue block to convert value-periodicity into a fixed index shift.
Misleading if detached from the proof: pairwise intersection alone does not imply finite constraint stabilization; the causal greedy order and arithmetic descent are essential.
Misleading if used alone: finite computational trace checks support the lemma but cannot establish its universal quantifiers or exact global periodicity.
